Who we are

One group, eight fields, a shared interest in what plants and natural resources can do.

NatPro is a research group at Universiti Teknologi Malaysia that brings together researchers in chemistry, plant science, biotechnology, genetics, molecular biopharming and nutrition.

The group is organised around eight research core areas and works across the boundaries between them — chemists profiling natural products alongside plant scientists developing the material those compounds come from, and nutrition researchers testing where they can be applied.

NatPro / About

About NatPro

The Natural Products (NatPro) Research Group at Universiti Teknologi Malaysia.

Introduction

A group defined by the range of its members

NatPro is organised around eight research core areas: natural product chemistry, therapeutic molecules, plant breeding and tissue culture, genetic transformation, biodiversity, nutrigenomics, animal nutrition and genetics.

Its members are chemists, plant scientists, geneticists, biotechnologists and nutrition researchers based at Universiti Teknologi Malaysia. That mix is the point: natural-product work rarely sits inside one discipline, and the group is set up so that expertise in profiling a compound, producing the plant material, transforming it and testing its use in nutrition can be brought together within one research group.

The eight core areas

Research philosophy

From natural resources to biological application

A conceptual view of how the group's expertise fits together. It is a map of what NatPro can cover collectively, not a claim that every project runs through every stage.

01

Natural resources

Plants and other natural sources, and the biodiversity they come from.

02

Scientific investigation

Chemical profiling, bioassay, organic synthesis and molecular docking.

03

Bioactive and therapeutic molecules

Identifying and working with the compounds themselves.

04

Plant and molecular biotechnology

Plant breeding, tissue culture, genetic transformation and molecular biopharming.

05

Nutrition and biological applications

Nutrigenomics and animal nutrition.
